title: Chief Executive Officer, Girls Leadership: Remote US-Based Executive Job Paying Up to $200,000
summary: The Chief Executive Officer, Girls Leadership opportunity offers an experienced nonprofit or social-impact executive the chance to lead a national organization focused on helping girls and gender-expansive youth develop confidence, leadership, social-emotional skills and the ability to use their voices. The recruitment is being managed by Carrington Talent Group on behalf of Girls Leadership , a nonprofit organization that works with the adults who shape girls daily lives, including teachers, coaches, counselors and family service providers. The organization provides these adults with training and tools to create environments in which girls can develop their voices, trust their power and become leaders. The position is a full-time, senior executive role and is described as remote and US-based. The successful candidate will report to the Board of Directors and lead a fully remote team dedicated to the well-being of girls and gender-expansive youth. The priority application deadline is October 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM ET . About Girls Leadership Girls Leadership is a nonprofit organization focused on creating environments where girls can develop leadership, confidence and social-emotional skills. The organization works indirectly as well as directly with young people by equipping influential adults in girls lives with the knowledge and tools needed to support their development. According to the organization, its work is built around three distinctive approaches: Working through influential adults: Girls Leadership works with teachers, coaches, counselors, family service providers and other adults who influence girls daily experiences. This approach is intended to multiply the organization s impact across classrooms, teams and communities. Social and emotional learning: Social and emotional learning (SEL) forms the foundation of the organization s educational approach. Co-design with marginalized girls: The organization develops its programs and partnerships with the most marginalized girls in mind, with the stated goal of creating approaches that can serve girls more broadly and effectively. These principles are central to the CEO position because the incoming leader will be expected to guide the organization s strategy, strengthen its national profile and expand its reach. About the Chief Executive Officer Opportunity Girls Leadership s Board of Directors is seeking a new Chief Executive Officer to lead the organization s next phase of growth and impact. The organization describes itself as a $2 million national organization and is looking for an executive who can provide strategic leadership while also strengthening fundraising, organizational sustainability, partnerships and national influence. The CEO will be expected to combine several areas of leadership, including: Organizational strategy Financial oversight Fundraising and revenue development Program development External relations Partnership development Team leadership Board engagement Organizational culture Operational effectiveness National thought leadership The position therefore requires more than traditional administrative management. The successful candidate will be expected to serve as a visible representative of Girls Leadership and help position the organization within the broader field of girls social-emotional development and youth well-being. What Will the CEO Be Expected to Do? The responsibilities are divided into several major areas. 1. Strategic Leadership and Organizational Effectiveness The CEO will work with the Board to establish a multi-year strategy and operating model for the organization s next phase of growth and impact. Key responsibilities include: Establishing strategic priorities in partnership with the Board. Translating organizational vision into an executable strategy. Establishing clear priorities, metrics and accountability. Maintaining executive oversight of financial health. Ensuring organizational resources are aligned with priorities and long-term sustainability. Strengthening Girls Leadership s value proposition. Positioning the organization within the wider youth-serving landscape. Improving organizational systems and decision-making across strategy, fundraising, programs, operations, finance and partnerships. This means the CEO will have significant responsibility for ensuring that the organization s mission is translated into practical organizational priorities and sustainable operations. 2. Fundraising, Revenue Expansion and Thought Leadership Fundraising and revenue development are major components of the role. The CEO will work with the Chief Development Officer, Board and other stakeholders to expand and diversify Girls Leadership s funding base. This includes developing relationships with: Individual donors Family offices Regional and national philanthropic organizations Corporate partners Existing funding partners Schools and school districts National partners Public funding sources The CEO will also explore additional earned-income opportunities, including school and district contracts and national partnerships. In addition, the CEO will serve as the organization s chief external ambassador and storyteller . This involves: Building relationships with important external partners. Increasing the organization s national profile. Communicating Girls Leadership s work to external audiences. Positioning the organization as a leader in social-emotional development and the well-being of girls and gender-expansive youth. 3. People Management and Team Development The CEO will lead a fully remote, values-driven team. The current team consists of 10 full-time employees , including three direct reports and seven indirect reports, as well as part-time Training Facilitators and external consultants. Responsibilities include: Inspiring and supporting the team. Coaching high-performing employees. Hiring additional team members where necessary. Developing existing staff. Strengthening an inclusive organizational culture. Ensuring diverse perspectives are actively considered in decision-making. Building a data-informed and learning-oriented organizational culture. Using evidence and feedback to improve organizational performance. The CEO will therefore have a significant people-leadership responsibility in addition to strategic and financial responsibilities. 4. Governance and Board Development The CEO will work closely with the Board of Directors to support effective governance and strategic oversight. Key responsibilities include: Maintaining an effective partnership with the Board. Supporting shared accountability for organizational outcomes. Helping cultivate a high-functioning governance culture. Supporting Board recruitment and development. Helping ensure that the Board has the skills and perspectives needed to advance Girls Leadership s work. Providing the Board with timely and accurate information concerning organizational performance. Reporting on financial health and emerging organizational risks. The CEO will therefore serve as an important connection between organizational management and Board governance. Required Experience and Skills The job listing sets out several specific requirements for candidates. Enterprise-Level Leadership Experience Candidates should have experience serving as an enterprise-level leader of a nonprofit organization or similar platform , with responsibility for areas such as: Organizational strategy Finance and operations Fundraising and revenue Programs The position requires substantial executive-level experience rather than an entry-level or mid-career management background. At Least Seven Years of Executive Leadership Experience Applicants must have at least seven years of enterprise-level executive leadership experience in the nonprofit or social-impact sector . This is one of the explicit requirements listed by the employer. Fundraising and Revenue Generation Candidates should have a demonstrated record of fundraising and revenue generation, including experience with six- and seven-figure gifts . This requirement reflects the significant fundraising and organizational revenue responsibilities attached to the CEO position. Experience Leading Organizations Through Growth and Transition The successful candidate should have demonstrated experience leading an organization through periods of transition and growth. The employer is looking for someone capable of balancing: Mission impact Program quality Organizational culture Financial sustainability within a complex nonprofit environment. Commitment to Gender and Racial Equity The position requires a deep commitment to advancing gender and racial equity . The listing states that this can be demonstrated through lived experience and/or a deep personal or professional connection to the communities Girls Leadership serves and the issues affecting girls and gender-expansive youth. Values-Driven Leadership Candidates should have experience leading a values-driven organization. Girls Leadership identifies its values as: Authentic Communication Courageous Growth Belonging Inclusion Play Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate experience working within an organizational culture grounded in clearly articulated values. Financial Management The CEO should understand key areas of nonprofit financial management, including: Cash-flow management Operating reserves Budgeting Forecasting Long-term organizational sustainability Travel Requirement Although the position is remote, regular domestic travel may be required . Travel may be associated with conferences, team gatherings, fundraising activities and other organizational responsibilities. Preferred Experience In addition to the required qualifications, Girls Leadership identifies several areas of experience that would be advantageous. Preferred experience includes: Youth development K–12 education Youth sports Girl-serving organizations Related youth-serving fields K–12 leadership Social and emotional learning frameworks Earned-revenue models in education or youth-serving nonprofits Partnerships with schools and school districts Candidates who have worked across several of these areas may be particularly well positioned to demonstrate relevance to the organization s mission and operating environment. Salary and Compensation The advertised base salary for the Chief Executive Officer position is: $170,000–$200,000 per year The listing states that compensation will be determined in relation to experience. The position also comes with a benefits package. Benefits Include Health Insurance Girls Leadership covers 99% of the employee premium for the employer-selected health insurance plan . Dental and Vision Optional dental and vision coverage is available. Paid Time Off The benefits package includes: Two weeks of paid time off One week of paid sick leave 11 paid holidays Four additional weeks of paid office closure each year The office closure consists of two weeks in July and two weeks in December. Retirement Plan A 401(k) retirement plan is available after one year of service. Phone and Internet Support The organization provides a monthly phone and internet stipend . Remote Work Arrangement Girls Leadership operates as a fully remote organization , with team members working across the United States. The job listing states that a majority of the current team is based in the Bay Area and New York . Although the role is remote, candidates should note that regular domestic travel is expected as part of the position. The application also asks candidates to confirm that they are willing and able to meet the travel requirement. Application Requirements The online application requires candidates to provide several pieces of information. Applicants are asked to submit: First name Last name Email address Phone number Address Resume LinkedIn profile URL The application also asks candidates to confirm their US work authorization status and whether they will require employment visa sponsorship. Candidates must also respond to specific questions concerning their qualifications and connection to Girls Leadership s mission. Mission and Equity Question Applicants are asked to explain, in 250 words or fewer , how their professional and/or lived experience demonstrates their commitment to work at the intersection of gender, race, identity and power and to supporting girls and gender-expansive youth. Fundraising Question Candidates must also briefly describe their fundraising and/or revenue-building outcomes, including specific experience securing gifts from: High-net-worth individuals Foundations Corporations This response is also limited to 250 words . These questions mean that applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their leadership record with concrete examples rather than relying only on a general description of their professional background. Equal Opportunity and Diversity Girls Leadership states that it is committed to equal opportunity for all persons regardless of: Sex Age Race Ethnicity Color Religion Creed National origin Marital status Gender expression Disability Sexual orientation The organization also states that it actively seeks a diverse pool of candidates from different backgrounds who share its mission and vision. The application contains optional demographic questions concerning gender and race/ethnicity. The listing states that these questions are requested for government Equal Employment Opportunity and/or Affirmative Action reporting purposes and are not required. Who Should Consider Applying? This position is designed for an experienced senior executive rather than an early-career professional. It may be relevant to leaders with substantial experience in areas such as: Nonprofit executive leadership Social-impact organizations Youth development Education Girls leadership and empowerment Social-emotional learning Youth-serving organizations Fundraising and philanthropy Organizational strategy Nonprofit financial management School and district partnerships Program leadership Organizational growth and transformation However, applicants should compare their experience directly with the employer s stated requirements, particularly the seven-year enterprise-level executive leadership requirement , fundraising record and nonprofit/social-impact leadership experience. Important Application Considerations Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should carefully consider several aspects of the position. 1. Demonstrate executive-level leadership The position requires at least seven years of enterprise-level executive leadership experience. Candidates should clearly demonstrate the scale and scope of organizations, teams, budgets, programs and responsibilities they have led. 2. Highlight fundraising outcomes Fundraising is a central part of the position. Candidates should provide concrete examples of revenue generation and fundraising success, including experience with significant gifts. 3. Connect experience to the mission The application specifically asks candidates about their professional and/or lived experience related to gender, race, identity and power. Applicants should therefore be prepared to explain their connection to Girls Leadership s mission clearly and specifically. 4. Demonstrate financial leadership Because the CEO will oversee organizational financial health, applicants should demonstrate experience with budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, reserves and long-term financial sustainability. 5. Be prepared for remote leadership and travel The organization is fully remote, but the position includes regular domestic travel. Applicants should make sure they can meet both requirements. Application Deadline The priority application deadline is October 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM Eastern Time (ET) . Candidates interested in the position should submit their applications by the stated deadline. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the Carrington Talent Group recruitment platform . Candidates should prepare their: Resume LinkedIn profile information Professional contact information Evidence of enterprise-level executive leadership Fundraising and revenue-generation examples Explanation of their connection to Girls Leadership s mission Information concerning US work authorization Confirmation of their ability to meet the domestic travel requirement The application specifically asks candidates whether they are authorized to work in the United States and whether they now or in the future require employment visa sponsorship. Visit HERE for more information about the Chief Executive Officer, Girls Leadership. Conclusion The Chief Executive Officer, Girls Leadership position presents an opportunity for an experienced nonprofit or social-impact executive to lead a national organization focused on girls leadership, social-emotional development and the well-being of girls and gender-expansive youth. The role combines strategic leadership, fundraising, organizational development, financial oversight, team management, Board engagement and external representation . The successful candidate will be expected to guide Girls Leadership through its next phase of growth while strengthening its financial sustainability, national profile and reach among educators, coaches and youth-serving organizations. The position is fully remote within the United States, with regular domestic travel required. It offers a stated base salary of $170,000 to $200,000 , together with health insurance, paid time off, retirement benefits and a monthly phone and internet stipend. Candidates should pay particular attention to the stated requirements, including at least seven years of enterprise-level executive leadership experience in the nonprofit or social-impact sector , demonstrated fundraising and revenue-generation success, organizational growth experience, financial management knowledge and a strong connection to the mission of Girls Leadership. The priority application deadline is October 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM ET . Interested candidates should review the complete position requirements and prepare their application materials before submitting their application through the official recruitment platform. title: Atlassian Foundation Open Call for Proposals 2026 – Up to US$1 Million for Education Initiatives
summary: Atlassian Foundation Open Call for Proposals 2026 The Atlassian Foundation Open Call for Proposals 2026 is now open for registered nonprofit organisations working as part of collective action initiatives to improve education for disadvantaged learners in the AI era . The Atlassian Foundation is deploying US$8 million over the next two years to help disadvantaged learners thrive in the AI era. Through this open call, each selected partnership can receive up to US$1 million over two years , alongside opportunities for peer-to-peer learning and optional access to Atlassian teamwork tools, support and resources. 📅 Applications open: 1 October 2026 (AEST) 📅 Applications close: 30 October 2026 (11:59 pm AEDT) 💰 Funding: Up to US$1 million over two years 🌍 Eligible applicants: Registered nonprofit organisations globally 🎯 Focus: Education, disadvantaged learners, collective action and the AI era 🚀 Funded work begins: May or June 2027 🔗 Apply and learn more: Atlassian Foundation Open Call Atlassian Foundation Open Call for Proposals 2026 The Atlassian Foundation focuses on education because it’s the most empowering force in the world – it’s the key to breaking cycles of poverty and disadvantage. But that key is slipping out of reach for far too many. UNESCO estimates that more than 250 million children are out of school. And for those in the classroom, learning isn’t guaranteed: 57% of children worldwide (nearly one billion) lack the basic skills they need for the era they’re growing up in. AI can expand access and accelerate learning. It can also widen inequality where it lands unevenly. No single organisation can tackle a challenge this complex. That’s why the Atlassian Foundation is backing collective action : coordinated efforts by multiple players to solve shared problems at scale. Atlassian’s mission is to unleash the potential of every team, so we’re uniquely positioned to power these efforts. We’ve spent 20+ years learning what makes teams work well together, and we’re offering that expertise – plus our funding, tools and hands-on support – to help collective action initiatives drive greater impact. We believe a better world is built with better teamwork, and collective action is teamwork at its most ambitious. Together, we want to shape a future where emerging technology closes gaps for learners the current system leaves behind, rather than widening them. About This Open Call What We Are Looking For In this open call, we’re seeking partnerships with collective action initiatives that are working to improve education for disadvantaged learners in the AI era . We’re inviting applications from initiatives that meet all three of these criteria: Direct relief of disadvantage: Work that directly relieves poverty or disadvantage for a clearly identified beneficiary group (not the general public). Collective action: Multiple players working together – through shared goals, delivery learning. Read more about how we define collective action . Evolving education in the AI era: Initiatives helping education evolve so emerging technology closes gaps for disadvantaged learners rather than widening them. This call is not about AI for AI s sake. It is about how the education sector, at all levels, responds to this seismic technological shift (and may include deliberate, reasoned choices not to use AI). Who Can Apply? The call is open globally to registered nonprofit organisations working as part of a collective action initiative . Applicants from countries under international sanctions are not eligible. Please see our eligibility checklist before starting your application. APPLY NOW What Our Partners Will Receive Each partnership will include: Funding Selected partners can receive up to US$1 million over two years , capped at 25% of your lead organisation s operating budget for the same period . A Learning Cohort Funded partners join a cohort that fosters peer-to-peer knowledge exchange . Your budget should include funding for at least one person from your initiative to travel to the United States or Australia in 2027/2028 to participate in cohort activities. Non-Financial Support Optional non-financial support includes free access to Atlassian’s teamwork tools, support resources , tailored to your needs. Learn more at Atlassian for Nonprofits . Check Your Eligibility Check your eligibility Before you invest time in the full application, please check that your lead applicant can answer “yes” to every item on the checklist. Any “no” means your application will not pass the eligibility stage. 2. Read the Application Guide Read the Application Guide It has essential information you’ll need to complete your application. 3. Still Unsure? Attend a webinar . Ready to Apply? If your organisation is working as part of a collective action initiative focused on improving education for disadvantaged learners in the AI era , review the eligibility requirements and application guide before submitting your application. The Atlassian Foundation Open Call for Proposals 2026 offers selected partnerships up to US$1 million over two years , with additional opportunities for learning, collaboration and optional non-financial support. title: ECB Traineeship in International Policy Analysis 2027: €1,170 Monthly Grant and Accommodation Allowance in Frankfurt
summary: The European Central Bank (ECB) is inviting applications for a Traineeship in International Policy Analysis within its Directorate General International and European Relations. Based in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, this traineeship provides an opportunity for qualified candidates to gain practical experience in international finance, monetary economics, financial markets, data analysis, econometrics and international macroeconomics while working alongside experts at one of Europe’s key public institutions. The position is designed for candidates with academic backgrounds in economics, econometrics, finance, data engineering, data science, applied mathematics or related disciplines. Successful trainees will support analytical work involving international financial and monetary developments, contribute to research projects, work with complex databases and quantitative tools, and assist with the preparation of analytical materials. The traineeship provides a monthly grant of €1,170 plus an accommodation allowance , and the initial placement will last between four and six months, with the possibility of extension to a maximum of 12 months. Applications must be submitted by 20 October 2026 . ECB Traineeship in International Policy Analysis 2027 Overview Host institution: European Central Bank (ECB) Directorate: International European Relations Division: International Policy Analysis Division Opportunity: Traineeship in International Policy Analysis Contract type: Traineeship Location: Frankfurt am Main, Germany Working arrangement: Full time Monthly grant: €1,170 Additional support: Accommodation allowance Duration: Initially four to six months Possible extension: Up to 12 months in total Potential start periods: Spring 2027, late summer 2027 or autumn 2027, depending on the position Application deadline: 20 October 2026 Selection process: Online interview About the European Central Bank The European Central Bank is a major European institution responsible for important monetary and financial responsibilities within the euro area. Through its work, the ECB contributes to monetary and financial stability and supports the functioning of the European financial system. The International European Relations Directorate General is responsible for preparing policy positions for the ECB, the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks on international and European issues. Its work covers a wide range of international and European matters, excluding positions concerning the macroeconomic policies of the euro area and EU Member States. The Directorate General has approximately 120 members of staff working on issues that require an understanding of European and global economic developments. For trainees interested in international economics, financial markets, monetary policy, economic research and quantitative analysis, the environment provides exposure to policy-oriented work conducted within a major European public institution. About the International Policy Analysis Division The successful trainee will join the International Policy Analysis Division , which focuses on issues that have systemic importance for the global economy and international monetary and financial systems. The division covers a broad range of subjects related to the international financial architecture and global economic developments. Areas of interest include: Global financial markets International financial systems Global monetary developments Exchange rates Commodities International spillovers Globalisation International macroeconomics International finance Quantitative economic analysis This makes the traineeship particularly relevant for candidates who want to develop practical experience in analysing international economic and financial developments. What the ECB Trainee Will Do The trainee will support the work of the International Policy Analysis Division and may be involved in several different analytical and research-related activities. The responsibilities can include: 1. Data Collection and Analysis Trainees will assist with collecting and analysing economic and financial data. This can involve gathering information from statistical agencies, publicly available sources and professional data providers. The work may require candidates to identify relevant datasets, organise information, analyse trends and prepare outputs that can support the division s research and policy work. 2. Preparing Tables and Charts The trainee may be responsible for transforming economic and financial data into clear tables, charts and other analytical outputs. These materials can be used to communicate findings and developments to colleagues and support presentations and policy-related discussions. Strong Excel skills and familiarity with quantitative analysis will therefore be important for the role. 3. Preparing Presentations The trainee may assist in preparing presentations related to international financial and monetary developments. This could involve collecting relevant information, analysing datasets, producing charts and tables, and presenting complex economic information in a structured and accessible way. 4. Maintaining and Developing Databases The position involves working with complex databases used to monitor global financial and monetary developments. The trainee may help maintain existing databases while also contributing to their further development and improvement. This responsibility is particularly relevant to applicants with experience in data management, data engineering, data science, economics or quantitative research. 5. Supporting Quantitative Tools and Modelling Infrastructure Trainees may also contribute to maintaining and further developing quantitative tools and modelling infrastructure. Candidates with programming or econometric software experience can apply their technical knowledge to practical economic and financial analysis. Relevant tools and programming languages can include: Python R MATLAB Stata EViews SQL Julia 6. Research Assistance Another important part of the traineeship is contributing to selected analytical projects by providing research assistance. This can give trainees practical exposure to policy-relevant research and allow them to work alongside experienced professionals dealing with international economic and financial issues. Professional Development Opportunities The ECB describes the traineeship as an opportunity to work closely with highly qualified experts on different tasks and projects in international finance and macroeconomics. Trainees will be assigned a mentor who will support their development during the placement. This mentoring arrangement can help participants develop their technical, analytical and professional capabilities while becoming familiar with the working environment of a major European institution. The traineeship also offers exposure to a multicultural workplace where colleagues from different European countries and professional backgrounds collaborate on international and European issues. Participants can therefore gain experience in areas such as: International finance Macroeconomic analysis Monetary economics Financial market analysis Economic research Data science Econometrics Quantitative modelling Database management Policy research Data visualisation Professional presentation Cross-cultural collaboration ECB Traineeship Qualifications and Requirements Applicants are expected to meet a number of academic, technical and language requirements. Educational Requirements Applicants must have a bachelor s degree or higher in one of the following areas or a related discipline: Economics Econometrics Finance Data engineering Data science Applied mathematics Related fields A master s degree is desirable, although it is not listed as an essential requirement. Candidates who are close to completing a master s degree may also be considered under the desired qualifications. Knowledge of Economics and Finance Candidates should have a sound understanding of at least one or more relevant areas, including: International finance Monetary economics Data science International macroeconomics The knowledge should be applicable to the type of analytical and research work carried out by the International Policy Analysis Division. Data Analysis Experience Applicants should have experience collecting data from sources such as: Statistical agencies Public databases Data providers Financial market data services The ECB specifically mentions providers such as LSEG, Bloomberg and Haver Analytics, as well as other market data services. Experience analysing this information is also relevant to the role. Programming and Econometric Software Applicants must have intermediate knowledge of one or more programming languages and/or econometric software packages. Examples listed by the ECB include: MATLAB R Stata EViews Python SQL Julia Candidates who can demonstrate practical experience using these tools for economic, financial, statistical or data-related work may be particularly aligned with the technical requirements of the position. Microsoft Office and Excel Applicants are expected to have advanced knowledge of the Microsoft Office package, particularly Microsoft Excel . Because the position involves data collection, analysis, tables, charts and presentations, strong spreadsheet and data-management capabilities are important. Language Requirements Language ability is another important requirement for this traineeship. Applicants must have: Advanced C1-level English , according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages; and Intermediate B1-level knowledge of at least one other official language of the European Union. The language requirement therefore extends beyond English, with applicants expected to demonstrate knowledge of another official EU language at the specified level. Desirable Qualifications In addition to the essential requirements, the ECB identifies several qualifications and characteristics that are desirable. These include: Master s Degree A master s degree in economics, econometrics, finance, data engineering, data science, applied mathematics or a related field is desirable. Candidates who are close to completing a master s degree may also be considered. Interest in Applied and Policy-Relevant Research Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in research that has practical policy relevance. The role is not limited to theoretical academic work. It involves using quantitative analysis and economic information to support work on international and financial issues. Quantitative Analysis A proven ability to conduct quantitative analyses is desirable. Applicants who have used statistical, econometric or programming techniques in academic projects, research, professional assignments or other relevant activities may be able to demonstrate this capability. Statistical and Econometric Knowledge A sound understanding of statistical and econometric techniques for data analysis is also desirable. This may include experience working with economic datasets, statistical modelling, econometric analysis, forecasting or other quantitative research methods. Personal and Professional Competencies Beyond academic qualifications and technical skills, the ECB is looking for candidates who demonstrate curiosity, willingness to learn and the ability to work collaboratively. Successful applicants should be interested in developing their ability to analyse complex information and should be comfortable working with colleagues who have different perspectives and areas of expertise. The ECB highlights qualities such as: Curiosity Eagerness to learn Analytical thinking Collaboration Teamwork Ability to understand complex information Awareness of stakeholder needs Willingness to identify areas for improvement Ability to propose alternative solutions Motivation to contribute to the ECB s mission Interest in working in a multicultural European environment Applicants should also be motivated to contribute to the work of a public institution serving citizens of the European Union. Duration of the ECB Traineeship The initial traineeship will last between four and six months . Depending on the circumstances and the applicable arrangements, the traineeship may be extended to a maximum of 12 months in total . The ECB indicates that starting dates can vary depending on the position. Some traineeships may begin in spring 2027 , while others may start in late summer or autumn 2027 . Applicants should therefore review the specific information provided during the recruitment process regarding the expected starting period. Financial Support and Accommodation Allowance Selected trainees will receive a trainee grant of €1,170 per month . In addition to the monthly grant, the ECB states that an accommodation allowance is available, subject to the applicable conditions. This financial support is intended to assist trainees during their placement in Frankfurt am Main. Applicants should consult the ECB s official traineeship conditions for the complete details regarding the grant, accommodation allowance and other applicable conditions. Location: Frankfurt am Main, Germany The traineeship will take place in Frankfurt am Main, Germany , one of Europe s major financial centres. Working in Frankfurt provides trainees with an opportunity to gain experience in an international financial environment while working within the European Central Bank. The role is full time and requires successful candidates to work as part of the International Policy Analysis Division. Application and Selection Process Candidates interested in this traineeship must complete the ECB s application process before the stated deadline. The recruitment process for this position will include an online interview . Applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates how their education, technical skills, research experience and language abilities correspond with the requirements of the position. Candidates should pay particular attention to demonstrating relevant experience in: International finance Economics or econometrics Data analysis Financial or economic databases Programming Statistical or econometric software Excel Quantitative research International macroeconomics Reserve List for Other Traineeship Opportunities An additional feature of the recruitment process is the ECB s reserve list. Candidates who are not selected for this particular position but are still considered suitable may be placed on a reserve list for 12 months from the application closing date . Individuals on the reserve list may subsequently be considered for other traineeship positions within the ECB during that period. Being placed on the reserve list does not mean that an applicant has been selected for another position, but it may allow the ECB to consider suitable candidates for other traineeship opportunities. Who Can Apply for the ECB International Policy Analysis Traineeship? The opportunity is open to EU nationals who are eligible for the ECB s traineeship programme . Applicants should also meet the academic, technical and language requirements specified for the position. Academic Profile Suitable candidates should generally have: A bachelor s degree or higher in economics, econometrics, finance, data engineering, data science, applied mathematics or a related field. A master s degree or near-completion of a master s degree is desirable but not essential according to the listed requirements. Technical Profile Candidates should have: Knowledge of international finance, monetary economics, data science or international macroeconomics. Experience with data collection and/or data analysis. Intermediate knowledge of at least one relevant programming language or econometric software package. Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel. Knowledge of statistical and econometric techniques is desirable. Language Profile Applicants need: C1-level English; and B1-level knowledge of at least one other official EU language. Geographic Eligibility The ECB specifically states that EU nationals eligible for its traineeship programme can apply. The opportunity is therefore not presented as a general worldwide traineeship open to applicants from every country. Applicants should verify their eligibility under the ECB s traineeship programme before submitting an application. Diversity and Inclusion The ECB states that it is an inclusive employer and seeks to reflect the diversity of the population it serves. The institution encourages applications irrespective of characteristics including: Age Disability Ethnicity Gender Gender identity Race Religious beliefs Sexual orientation Other characteristics These statements form part of the ECB s broader commitment to an inclusive working environment. Why This Traineeship Can Be Relevant for Economics and Data Professionals The ECB International Policy Analysis traineeship combines economics, finance, data and policy analysis in a professional institutional environment. Unlike a programme focused exclusively on one technical discipline, the role can expose trainees to several interconnected areas of international economic analysis. For candidates interested in international financial markets, the opportunity may provide practical exposure to the analysis of global financial and monetary developments. For data-oriented candidates, responsibilities involving databases, programming, quantitative tools and data analysis can provide an opportunity to apply technical skills to economic questions. For economics and finance graduates, the position offers an opportunity to work on analytical projects connected to international finance and macroeconomics. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants can improve the clarity of their application by carefully connecting their experience to the specific requirements of the traineeship. A strong application should clearly demonstrate relevant academic preparation and practical experience rather than simply listing qualifications. Candidates may consider highlighting: Relevant academic coursework in economics, finance, econometrics, monetary economics, international economics, mathematics or data science. Research projects involving economic, financial or international datasets. Programming experience using Python, R, MATLAB, Stata, EViews, SQL, Julia or other relevant tools. Data analysis experience , including collection, cleaning, processing, visualisation and interpretation. Excel skills , especially experience working with large datasets, formulas, charts, tables and analytical models. Econometric experience , where applicable. Experience with financial or economic databases and data providers. Quantitative research projects that demonstrate analytical ability. International economics or finance knowledge relevant to the division s work. Language capabilities , particularly English and another official EU language. Applicants should also ensure that their information is accurate and that their application reflects the requirements stated in the official vacancy. APPLY HERE How to Apply Interested candidates should apply through the European Central Bank s official careers platform and review the detailed requirements and application instructions before submitting their application. Applicants can also review the ECB s information about traineeships, benefits and the application process through its official careers resources. Visit HERE to learn more about the ECB Traineeship in International Policy Analysis 2027. Important Deadline The application deadline for the ECB Traineeship in International Policy Analysis is: 20 October 2026 Applicants should submit their applications before the closing date and allow sufficient time to complete all required application steps. Conclusion The ECB Traineeship in International Policy Analysis offers an opportunity for eligible EU nationals with backgrounds in economics, econometrics, finance, data science, data engineering, applied mathematics and related fields to gain practical experience in international economic and financial analysis. The role combines data analysis, quantitative research, database management, programming, economic research and policy-oriented work. Trainees will work within the International Policy Analysis Division of the ECB s Directorate General International and European Relations and will have opportunities to collaborate with experienced professionals and receive mentoring. With a €1,170 monthly trainee grant plus an accommodation allowance , an initial duration of four to six months and the possibility of extension to up to 12 months, the traineeship provides structured professional experience in Frankfurt am Main. Candidates who meet the academic, technical and language requirements and are eligible under the ECB s traineeship programme should carefully review the official vacancy and submit their applications by 20 October 2026 . title: WTPO Awards 2027: Global Trade Promotion Organizations Invited to Showcase Excellence in Export Development, Technology and Sustainable Trade
summary: The WTPO Awards 2027 are now open, offering Trade Promotion Organizations (TPOs) from around the world an opportunity to showcase innovative initiatives that strengthen exports, support businesses, improve SME competitiveness, and contribute to sustainable economic development. Organized through the International Trade Centre (ITC) , the WTPO Awards have been bringing together the global trade promotion community for nearly three decades. The 2027 edition provides participating organizations with opportunities to gain international recognition, demonstrate measurable impact, exchange good practices, and connect with trade promotion leaders from around the world. The 2027 awards feature three main categories covering partnerships, technology, and inclusive and sustainable trade. A new TPO Trailblazer Award has also been introduced for organizations implementing concrete changes based on their TPO Roadmaps for Excellence. The Stage 1 application deadline is November 15, 2026 . What Are the WTPO Awards 2027? The WTPO Awards recognize outstanding Trade Promotion Organizations that demonstrate excellence in developing and implementing initiatives designed to strengthen international trade. For nearly 30 years, the International Trade Centre has brought TPOs together to celebrate achievements, exchange knowledge, share successful practices, and strengthen the international trade promotion community. The awards focus on initiatives that can demonstrate meaningful contributions to areas such as: Export development SME competitiveness Digital transformation Partnerships and collaboration Inclusive economic growth Sustainable trade Implementation of the UN Sustainable Development Goals Innovative approaches to trade promotion The awards therefore provide a platform for TPOs to demonstrate how their initiatives are addressing practical challenges faced by exporters and businesses. WTPO Awards 2027 at a Glance Feature Details Opportunity WTPO Awards 2027 Organizer International Trade Centre (ITC) Target participants Trade Promotion Organizations Main award categories Three Special distinction TPO Trailblazer Award Stage 1 deadline November 15, 2026 Qualifying applicants confirmed December 21, 2026 Stage 2 deadline February 26, 2027 Shortlisted finalists announced May 4, 2027 Winners announced May 25, 2027 Main event Global SME Ministerial TPO Leadership Dialogue Geographic scope Global What Is a Trade Promotion Organization? Trade Promotion Organizations, commonly known as TPOs , work to support businesses and strengthen their ability to participate in international markets. Depending on their national or regional mandate, TPOs may help businesses with activities such as: Export development Market access Internationalization Export readiness Trade information Business connections International market intelligence SME support Investment and trade promotion The WTPO Awards provide these organizations with a platform to showcase initiatives that have generated meaningful results in these areas. The Three WTPO Awards 2027 Categories The 2027 edition features three principal award categories. Organizations should consider which category most closely corresponds to the initiative they wish to submit. 1. Best Use of Partnerships The Best Use of Partnerships category recognizes initiatives that effectively use partnerships and collaborative networks to strengthen export development and increase impact. Trade promotion frequently requires cooperation between multiple stakeholders. These can include government institutions, private-sector organizations, business associations, financial institutions, international organizations, research institutions, and other partners. This category provides an opportunity for TPOs to demonstrate how collaboration has helped them achieve stronger results than they could have achieved independently. Examples of partnership-related approaches may include: Developing collaborative export programs Building networks that connect businesses with international markets Working with public and private-sector partners Establishing strategic collaborations Coordinating initiatives involving multiple stakeholders Using partnerships to expand the reach of trade promotion services Applicants should use their submission to demonstrate how partnerships contributed to the initiative s objectives and impact. 2. Best Use of Technology The Best Use of Technology category recognizes innovative digital solutions that improve productivity, service delivery, client engagement, and exporter support. Technology is increasingly transforming the way organizations interact with businesses and deliver trade-related services. TPOs using technology to make their services more accessible, efficient, responsive, or data-driven can use this category to showcase their initiatives. Potential areas may include: Digital exporter support platforms Online trade services Digital market intelligence Technology-enabled client engagement Digital tools for SMEs Online training and capacity building Digital systems that improve organizational productivity Technology that makes export services more accessible The emphasis is on how technology has been applied to improve outcomes for the organization and the businesses it supports. 3. Best Initiative for Inclusive and Sustainable Trade The Best Initiative for Inclusive and Sustainable Trade category recognizes initiatives that advance inclusive growth, sustainable trade, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) . This category provides an opportunity for TPOs to highlight programs that address broader economic, social, and environmental objectives alongside trade development. Relevant initiatives may demonstrate contributions toward: Inclusive economic growth Sustainable trade Sustainable business practices SME development Greater participation in international markets Broader economic opportunities Contributions to the UN Sustainable Development Goals Organizations considering this category should clearly explain how their initiative contributes to inclusive and sustainable development. Apply HERE New for 2027: TPO Trailblazer Award The WTPO Awards 2027 introduces a new distinction: the TPO Trailblazer Award . This award is separate from the three main WTPO Award categories. The Trailblazer Award recognizes TPOs that are turning commitments into concrete action by implementing changes aligned with their TPO Roadmaps for Excellence . These roadmaps were developed as an outcome of the 2025 TPO Leadership Dialogue . How Is the Trailblazer Award Different? The Trailblazer Award has several distinctions from the three main WTPO Awards: It has its own evaluation criteria. It follows a separate evaluation process. It is not assessed by the WTPO Awards jury. It is conferred by the Executive Director of the International Trade Centre . It focuses specifically on concrete changes associated with TPO Roadmaps for Excellence. Organizations can apply for both the main WTPO Awards and the Trailblazer Award. Importantly, the two applications are independent. Applying for one does not affect eligibility for the other. Learn more about the TPO Trailblazer Award What Is the TPO Leadership Dialogue? The TPO Leadership Dialogue is a high-level international forum that brings together leaders of national trade and investment promotion organizations as well as senior trade representatives from around the world. The Dialogue creates a space for participants to: Exchange experiences Discuss emerging challenges Explore opportunities in trade promotion Strengthen relationships Develop partnerships Share institutional experiences Discuss developments affecting trade promotion organizations The WTPO Awards finalists will be announced at the TPO Leadership Dialogue. The Dialogue also provides an opportunity for TPO leaders to interact with ministers, policymakers, and representatives of the private sector. Connection With the Global SME Ministerial The TPO Leadership Dialogue is held alongside the Global SME Ministerial . This creates an additional opportunity for trade promotion leaders to connect with: Ministers Policymakers Private-sector representatives Trade promotion organizations International stakeholders The combination of the Leadership Dialogue and Global SME Ministerial creates a setting for discussions connecting trade promotion with broader SME and trade policy priorities. A Global History of the WTPO Awards and Leadership Dialogue The WTPO Awards and TPO Leadership Dialogue have travelled across different regions of the world over the years. Previous host cities and editions include: 1996 — Cartagena, Colombia 1998 — Santiago, Chile 2000 — Marrakech, Morocco 2002 — Beijing, China 2004 — St. Julian s, Malta 2007 — Buenos Aires, Argentina 2008 — The Hague, Netherlands 2010 — Mexico City, Mexico 2012 — Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia 2014 — Dubai, UAE 2016 — Marrakech, Morocco 2018 — Paris, France 2022 — Accra, Ghana 2025 — Johannesburg, South Africa This history reflects the international nature of the WTPO community and the program s focus on bringing trade promotion organizations together across different regions. What Happened at the 2025 TPO Leadership Dialogue? The first TPO Leadership Dialogue in its new format took place on July 22, 2025 , alongside the inaugural Global SME Ministerial Meeting in Johannesburg, South Africa. The event concluded with a gala ceremony recognizing the WTPO Awards winners. The 2024 WTPO winners celebrated at the 2025 ceremony included: Business France Switzerland Global Enterprise ApexBrasil The runners-up included: PROCOMER ProDominicana NIPDB The previous edition provides context for the international recognition associated with the WTPO Awards. Why Should Trade Promotion Organizations Apply? Participation in the WTPO Awards is an opportunity for organizations to present their work to an international audience of trade promotion professionals and stakeholders. According to the program information, participating organizations can use the awards to: Gain International Recognition The awards provide a platform for organizations to showcase outstanding initiatives and achievements internationally. Demonstrate Impact Participation allows TPOs to demonstrate the results of their initiatives to governments, partners, stakeholders, and the wider trade promotion community. Benchmark Initiatives Organizations can compare their approaches and experiences with those of other TPOs from around the world. Share Innovative Practices The awards provide an opportunity to share approaches that other trade promotion organizations may find useful or adaptable. Increase Visibility Selected initiatives can receive exposure through ITC s international communication channels. Receive Expert Feedback The application process can provide feedback that organizations can use to strengthen future initiatives. Application Guide for the WTPO Awards 2027 Applicants are encouraged to download and review the official WTPO Awards 2027 Application Guide before preparing their submissions. The guide provides important information about: Eligibility requirements Application procedures Evaluation criteria Frequently asked questions Submission requirements Download the WTPO Awards 2027 Application Guide Reviewing the guide carefully is particularly important because the application process involves multiple stages. September 21, 2026 — Call for Applications The WTPO Awards 2027 officially launched and applications opened. November 15, 2026 — Stage 1 Application Deadline This is the first major deadline for organizations interested in participating. Deadline: November 15, 2026 Organizations should ensure their Stage 1 application is completed and submitted before the deadline. December 21, 2026 — Qualifying Applicants Confirmed Applicants who meet the qualifying requirements are expected to be confirmed and informed on this date. February 26, 2027 — Stage 2 Application Deadline Qualified applicants proceed to the second stage, with the Stage 2 application deadline scheduled for February 26, 2027 . May 4, 2027 — Shortlisted Finalists Announced The shortlisted finalists are scheduled to be announced on May 4, 2027 . May 25, 2027 — Winners Announced The winners will be announced at the Global SME Ministerial and TPO Leadership Dialogue on May 25, 2027 . How to Prepare a Strong WTPO Awards Application Trade Promotion Organizations preparing an application should carefully consider how their initiative aligns with the relevant award category. A strong preparation process can include the following steps. 1. Identify the Initiative Clearly define the initiative that the organization wants to showcase. The initiative should be connected to the objectives of one of the award categories. 2. Select the Most Appropriate Category Consider whether the initiative most closely relates to: Partnerships Technology Inclusive and sustainable trade Organizations applying separately for the Trailblazer Award should also review its specific requirements. 3. Demonstrate Results Applicants should be prepared to explain what the initiative achieved and how its impact can be demonstrated. Relevant evidence may include measurable outcomes, changes in service delivery, improvements for exporters, partnerships established, or other appropriate indicators. 4. Explain the Innovation or Approach The application should clearly communicate what makes the initiative distinctive and how it addresses a particular trade promotion challenge. 5. Connect the Initiative With Broader Objectives Depending on the category, applicants should explain connections to export development, SME competitiveness, digital transformation, inclusion, sustainability, or the SDGs. 6. Review the Official Evaluation Criteria Before submitting an application, organizations should consult the official application guide and make sure their submission addresses the applicable evaluation criteria. How to Apply for the WTPO Awards 2027 Organizations interested in applying can begin by reviewing the official application guide and then accessing the online application platform. Step 1: Review the Application Guide Understand the eligibility requirements, categories, evaluation process, and submission requirements. Step 2: Select Your Award Category Choose the category that best corresponds to the initiative being submitted. Step 3: Prepare the Application Collect the necessary information and supporting material required for Stage 1. Step 4: Submit Before November 15, 2026 Ensure that the Stage 1 application is submitted before the official deadline. Step 5: Monitor the Selection Process Qualifying applicants are scheduled to be informed on December 21, 2026, followed by the Stage 2 application process. Apply for the WTPO Awards 2027 How to Apply for the TPO Trailblazer Award Organizations interested in the newly introduced Trailblazer Award have a separate application process. The Trailblazer Award application is independent of the three main WTPO Awards categories. Organizations can therefore apply for both programs without one application affecting the eligibility of the other. Download the TPO Trailblazer Award Application Guide Apply for the TPO Trailblazer Award Previous WTPO Award Winners The WTPO Awards have previously recognized organizations for their achievements in trade promotion. The 2024 winners recognized at the 2025 gala ceremony were: Business France Switzerland Global Enterprise ApexBrasil Their participation demonstrates the international scope of the awards and the variety of organizations involved in the global trade promotion community. Frequently Asked Questions About WTPO Awards 2027 What are the WTPO Awards? The WTPO Awards recognize outstanding Trade Promotion Organizations that demonstrate excellence in export development and related areas. Who organizes the WTPO Awards? The awards are organized through the International Trade Centre (ITC) . Who can participate? The opportunity is designed for Trade Promotion Organizations rather than individual applicants. How many main award categories are there? title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027–28 at Lingnan University: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity for International Students
summary: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) 2027–28 offers an opportunity for outstanding students from around the world to pursue doctoral studies in Hong Kong. Lingnan University is among the participating universities that can nominate exceptional PhD applicants for consideration under the fellowship scheme. Established by the Research Grants Council (RGC) of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in 2009, the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme was created to attract high-achieving students from around the world to undertake PhD studies at Hong Kong universities. For the 2027–28 academic year , the scheme is accepting applications from 1 September 2026 until 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time for the initial RGC application. Applicants seeking admission to PhD programmes through the scheme must also complete their full university application by the university s stated deadline. At Lingnan University, the full application deadline for applicants applying through the HKPFS is 1 December 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Hong Kong Time . Late applications will not be accepted. What Is the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme? The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme is a doctoral fellowship initiative established by the Research Grants Council to attract outstanding students internationally to pursue full-time PhD studies at participating universities in Hong Kong. The scheme is designed for applicants who demonstrate strong academic and research potential as well as qualities that can contribute to their future academic, professional, and leadership development. The official RGC describes the scheme as being open to applicants seeking admission as new full-time PhD students , regardless of their country of origin, prior work experience, or ethnic background. Applicants are expected to demonstrate outstanding academic performance, research ability or potential, communication and interpersonal skills, and leadership abilities. For prospective doctoral students looking to undertake advanced research in Hong Kong, the HKPFS provides a route through which they can apply for both PhD admission and consideration for a competitive fellowship award. Lingnan University and the HKPFS Lingnan University is one of the universities participating in the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme. For the 2027–28 admission cycle, Lingnan University will assess applicants to its PhD programmes and nominate outstanding applicants for consideration for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowships. The selection process therefore involves more than simply submitting an application to Lingnan University. Applicants first complete the required initial application through the RGC s Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme system. They then submit a full PhD application to their selected university or universities. Lingnan University conducts its own selection of PhD applicants and nominates outstanding candidates for the fellowship. The RGC then uses selection panels to assess the nominations submitted by participating institutions. This means applicants should pay close attention to both the HKPFS application requirements and Lingnan University s PhD admission requirements . Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027–28 Funding One of the major features of the fellowship is its financial support. For the 2026–27 rate stated by Lingnan University, each fellowship awardee receives: HK$28,700 monthly stipend , subject to annual review Up to HK$14,400 per year for conference and research-related travel Fellowship support for a maximum period of three years Lingnan University s announcement further states that where an awardee has a normative study period of four years , the University will provide the same level of fellowship and conference/research-related travel allowance for the fourth year. The Research Grants Council currently states the annual fellowship value as HK$344,400 , equivalent to approximately HK$28,700 per month , together with a HK$14,400 annual conference and research-related travel allowance for up to three years. The RGC notes that the stipend is subject to annual review. What the Fellowship Funding Covers The financial package is designed to support doctoral researchers during their PhD studies. Monthly stipend Awardees receive a monthly stipend intended to provide financial support throughout the fellowship period. For the rate stated for 2026–27, the monthly amount is: HK$28,700 per month This corresponds to an annual stipend of: HK$344,400 per year Conference and research-related travel allowance In addition to the monthly stipend, awardees receive an annual allowance of up to: HK$14,400 per year This is intended for conference and research-related travel. Such funding can support doctoral researchers who need to participate in academic conferences, research activities, or other approved research-related travel. Potential fourth-year support at Lingnan The Lingnan University announcement contains an additional provision for PhD programmes with a normative study period of four years. For an awardee whose programme has a four-year normative study period, Lingnan University states that it will provide the same level of fellowship and conference/research-related travel allowance for the fourth year . Applicants should nevertheless confirm the applicable funding arrangements for their particular programme directly with Lingnan University. Who Can Apply for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme? The HKPFS has an international eligibility scope. The official Research Grants Council states that individuals seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at participating UGC-funded universities in Hong Kong may apply, irrespective of their country of origin, prior work experience, or ethnic background . This means the opportunity is not restricted to applicants from Hong Kong or a particular continent. Applicants from around the world can be considered, provided they satisfy the requirements of the fellowship and the specific PhD programme to which they apply. Academic and Professional Qualities Expected According to the RGC, applicants should demonstrate strength in several areas: Academic performance Research ability or research potential Communication and interpersonal skills Leadership abilities Academic excellence is the primary consideration in the fellowship selection process, while research potential, communication and interpersonal skills, and leadership abilities are also taken into account. Applicants should therefore present a strong academic and research profile rather than relying solely on their academic qualifications. Is the Fellowship Open to Applicants From Africa? Yes. The official HKPFS eligibility information states that applicants are eligible irrespective of their country of origin. Therefore, applicants from African countries , including applicants from countries such as Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and other African countries, can apply, provided they meet the relevant PhD programme admission requirements. The scheme is similarly open to applicants from other regions around the world. There is also no race or ethnic restriction stated by the RGC; its official eligibility statement specifically says eligibility applies irrespective of ethnic background. Relevant Fields and PhD Programmes The HKPFS is not limited to one academic discipline. The RGC assesses shortlisted applicants through two broad selection areas: Sciences, Medicine, Engineering and Technology This panel covers research areas within the broad fields of: Sciences Medicine Engineering Technology Humanities, Social Sciences and Business Studies The second broad area covers: Humanities Social sciences Business studies The specific PhD programmes available to applicants depend on the participating university and its programme offerings. Applicants should therefore identify a suitable PhD programme at Lingnan University and carefully review the programme-specific admission requirements before applying. How the HKPFS Application Process Works Applicants seeking the fellowship must complete the application process in stages. Step 1: Submit the Initial HKPFS Application Applicants must first submit an initial application through the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Electronic System (HKPFSES) operated by the Research Grants Council. For the 2027–28 cycle, the initial application period is: 1 September 2026 to 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time. Applicants who successfully complete the initial application receive an HKPFS reference number . This reference number is important because it is subsequently used when submitting the full application to the selected university or universities. Step 2: Submit the Full Application to Lingnan University After completing the initial RGC application, applicants must submit their full PhD application directly to Lingnan University. Lingnan University s application instructions specify that applicants should quote the reference number assigned by the RGC for verification. For the 2027–28 intake, applicants should select: “HK PhD Fellowship Scheme (2027-28)” as the application type in Lingnan University s Online Admission System. The full Lingnan University application must be submitted by: 1 December 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Hong Kong Time. Lingnan University explicitly states that no late application will be accepted . How Applicants Are Selected The selection process takes place at both the university and fellowship levels. First, Lingnan University conducts its own selection of applicants for its PhD programmes. The University then nominates outstanding applicants for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowships. After nominations are submitted, the RGC establishes selection panels to assess the nominated candidates. The official RGC information states that shortlisted applications are reviewed according to their broad academic area by one of two selection panels: Sciences, Medicine, Engineering and Technology Humanities, Social Sciences and Business Studies Individual universities may also conduct interviews as part of the assessment process. What Are the Selection Criteria? Academic excellence is the primary consideration in the fellowship selection process. The RGC also considers: Research ability and potential Communication and interpersonal skills Leadership abilities Applicants should therefore present evidence of both academic achievement and the ability to contribute meaningfully to research and the wider academic community. What Happens If You Do Not Receive the Fellowship? Not receiving the HKPFS fellowship does not necessarily mean that an applicant s PhD application at Lingnan University will automatically be rejected. Lingnan University states that applicants who are: nominated for the fellowship but are not finally awarded the fellowship, or not selected for nomination for the fellowship, may still be considered for admission as PhD students at Lingnan University and may take up places assigned to the University with Postgraduate Studentship awards . The broader RGC guidance similarly states that candidates who are not selected for the HKPFS may be accepted by participating universities for regular PhD admission and may receive postgraduate studentships, subject to the university s assessment and admission requirements. This creates a distinction between: admission to the PhD programme, and receiving the HKPFS fellowship. Applicants should therefore understand that the fellowship selection and ordinary university admission are related but distinct processes. Lingnan University Direct PhD Admission Option Lingnan University also offers a separate route for applicants who wish to apply directly to the University s PhD programmes rather than through the HKPFS. According to Lingnan University s 2027–28 admission information, PhD applicants can apply in two ways: Through the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Through Direct Admissions to the University Successful applicants through the direct admission route will normally receive a Postgraduate Studentship with a monthly stipend of HK$19,280 under the stated 2026–27 rate, with the amount subject to revision after confirmation of candidature. Applicants should select the appropriate application route carefully because the University states that applications cannot be transferred from one route to the other after submission. Application Limits Applicants should also pay attention to Lingnan University s application restrictions. Each applicant may apply for a maximum of two programmes . The University states that this restriction also applies where an applicant submits applications through both the HKPFS and Direct Admissions routes. The RGC similarly states that HKPFS applicants may choose up to two programmes or departments at one or two universities. Applicants must ensure that they select the correct application type and provide accurate and complete information. Lingnan University states that an application submitted through one route cannot later be transferred to the other route, and application fees paid are non-refundable and non-transferable. Important Integrity and Application Rules Applicants are expected to provide accurate and authentic information throughout the application process. Lingnan University states that false or misleading information or documents, dishonest conduct, plagiarism, and other forms of misconduct can result in consequences including disqualification, withdrawal of an admission offer, or termination of studies if the applicant has already been admitted. The University also states that falsification of documents is not tolerated and highlights Hong Kong s laws concerning forgery. Applicants and their representatives are also prohibited from offering advantages to University staff or members in relation to admission applications. Prospective applicants should therefore ensure that every document submitted is accurate, authentic, and properly prepared. Do Not Use Unauthorised Admission Agents Lingnan University s admission information contains an important warning concerning third-party recruitment. The University states that its School of Graduate Studies has not authorised any third party for admissions or recruitment work involving research postgraduate students . Applicants should therefore exercise caution if someone claims to represent Lingnan University or offers to guarantee admission or fellowship selection in exchange for payment. The safest approach is to use the official university and Research Grants Council application systems. Important Considerations for International Applicants Because the HKPFS accepts applicants regardless of country of origin, it is an international opportunity. However, international applicants must still satisfy the admission requirements of the specific university and PhD programme they select. The RGC explicitly notes that applicants are required to comply fully with the admission requirements of their selected universities and programmes. Therefore, being eligible to apply for the HKPFS does not automatically mean that an applicant meets the academic or programme-specific requirements for every PhD programme. Applicants should check: The specific PhD programme Academic qualifications required Research requirements Supporting documents Language requirements, where applicable Programme-specific deadlines University application procedures Any additional requirements imposed by the department or faculty Key Benefits of the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme The fellowship offers several major benefits to successful awardees. Financial Support Awardees receive a monthly stipend of HK$28,700 under the stated 2026–27 rate, subject to annual review. Research and Conference Travel Support Awardees receive up to HK$14,400 per year for conference and research-related travel. International PhD Study The scheme allows successful candidates from around the world to pursue doctoral studies at participating Hong Kong universities. Research Development PhD study provides an opportunity to undertake advanced research within a university environment and contribute to the applicant s academic and professional development. Potential Continued Support For Lingnan University programmes with a normative four-year study period, the University states that the same level of fellowship and travel allowance will be offered for the fourth year. Alternative Postgraduate Studentship Consideration Candidates who are not ultimately selected for the fellowship may still be considered for regular PhD admission and postgraduate studentship support, subject to the University s assessment. Key Dates for HKPFS 2027–28 Stage Date HKPFS application opens 1 September 2026 RGC initial application deadline 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon HKT Lingnan University full application deadline 1 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. HKT Academic year 2027–28 The RGC confirms that the 2027–28 HKPFS application period runs from 1 September 2026 to 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time . Step 1: Identify an appropriate PhD programme Review Lingnan University s available research postgraduate programmes and identify a PhD programme that matches your academic background and research interests. Step 2: Review programme requirements Check the specific admission requirements for the selected PhD programme. The RGC makes clear that applicants must comply with the requirements of their selected university and programme. Step 3: Submit the initial HKPFS application Submit the initial application through the official RGC HKPFS Electronic System.
